nodes.title: Bounded projectives and coefficient lifting
nodes.statement: For Λ=Z/ℓ^c and a finite downward-closed bound W, the perverse representing object P_W for the restricted geometric total-cohomology functor has a finite filtration with standard subquotients Δ_μ tensored with finite free Λ-modules. Thus P_W is ULA flat perverse and represents the restriction to Satake. Under Λ→Λ′ among the source coefficient rings its representing maps base change, so the bounded adjunction and its finite-projective fibres commute with coefficients. The multileg generator is the fusion product of the single-leg generators.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: For a maximal μ in W, adjunction against ∇_μ identifies the free coefficient module on its stratum. Self-injectivity of Z/ℓ^c makes the dual coefficient module free. Remove the maximal stratum and use induction on W.

The potential kernel K in the standard extension is killed by a uniform ℓ^a from the standard-to-costandard comparison. Repeat the construction over Z/ℓ^(c+a). The transition K′→K is zero by the torsion bound and flat standard term, while coefficient reduction makes it surjective. Hence K=0; this supplies the standard filtration without an integral decomposition theorem.

The stratum calculation and representing maps commute with reduction, so uniqueness of adjoints gives the coefficient comparison. Over disjoint legs tensor the adjunctions, then use the full-faithful ULA extension to obtain the multileg assertion.
acceptance: W={0} gives the tensor unit and L(V)=V.
The uniform exponent a is chosen before c; allowing an exponent depending on c would not prove the lifting argument.
No assertion that arbitrary integral perverse sheaves are semisimple is used.

sources.match: The representability proof supplies the maximal-stratum induction and the coefficient-lifting argument.

nodes.title: Split coequalizers for relative reconstruction
nodes.statement: For an F-split parallel pair u,v:A⇉B in Satake, form f=u−v in the ambient perverse heart. Its fibre cokernel is a direct summand of F(B) and is finite projective. VI.7.10 therefore constructs Q=coker(f) in the ULA flat-perverse subcategory. B→Q is the coequalizer there, F carries it to the split coequalizer, and F reflects such colimit cocones. Consequently the exact MC.6 relative reconstruction hypotheses are satisfied on each enlarged support bound.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: Use the F-split fork to split the fibre quotient and its image; apply VI.7.10 to the cokernel. A quotient of a bounded-support object has that support bound, and its finite-projective fibre gives the requisite flatness.

The Satake category is a full subcategory of the perverse category, so the ambient cokernel universal property restricts to it. Exactness of total cohomology identifies its fibre with the split quotient, establishing preservation.

Given any candidate cocone whose F-image is the coequalizer, compare it with Q. The induced map becomes an isomorphism under F; conservativity makes it an isomorphism in Satake, establishing reflection. This is the preservation-and-reflection input of Beck, not mere reflection of isomorphisms alone.
acceptance: A split epimorphism has its usual quotient.
An arbitrary perverse cokernel with nonprojective fibre is outside the assertion.
Compare the three separate pinned Beck classes rather than claiming they are interchangeable.

sources.match: The direct-summand criterion supplies the categorical coequalizers; the relative reconstruction theorem consumes them.

nodes.title: Finite pieces in adic reconstruction
nodes.statement: Write the Satake coordinate algebra as the filtered colimit of dual bounded fibres. For a fixed bound W the compatible finite-free systems (F_W X_W)^∨ over Z/ℓ^c lift to a finite-free Z_ℓ-module with the compatible structure maps. Construct the algebraic Hopf algebra over Z_ℓ by taking the filtered colimit of these lifted pieces, with tensor operations defined after enlarging bounds. Its reduction and rationalization give the reconstructed coefficient Hopf algebras. The algebraic coordinate ring is not defined as the unqualified inverse limit of the whole torsion coordinate rings.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: Use the bounded coefficient adjunction comparison before dualizing. Fixed finite rank and compatible basis lifting identify each piece with the inverse limit of its reductions.

For multiplication choose a common enlarged tensor-support bound, lift the finite-piece maps, and check identities modulo every ℓ^c. Finite-free separatedness proves the identities integrally. Pass to the filtered colimit only after this step.

Reduction commutes with filtered colimits and finite-projective duals. Tensor products handle the finite leg set; prime-to-p torsion rings decompose by CRT. Flatness follows from the filtered colimit of finite-free modules.
acceptance: For a torus recover Z_ℓ[X_*(T)] with finite Laurent sums.
The ℓ-adic completion of Z_ℓ[x,x^−1] contains convergent infinite Laurent sums; it is not substituted for the algebraic torus coordinate ring.
The empty leg set gives the coefficient ring with the unit Hopf structure.

sources.match: The coefficient and leg compatibilities are applied at the bounded representing objects, keeping the resulting group algebraic.

nodes.title: Geometric finite-type and connectedness tests
nodes.statement: On a geometric splitting fibre, the rational Satake category is semisimple with simples IC_μ indexed by dominant coweights. Finite generators of the dominant monoid and their duals tensor-generate this category under subquotients, so its Tannakian group is finite type. Any nontrivial simple has nonzero highest weight μ and tensor powers with distinct highest weights nμ, so it cannot generate a finite tensor subcategory. In characteristic zero the connectedness criterion therefore makes the group connected. The existing characteristic-zero reductive/linearly-reductive theorem then makes this finite-type group reductive. This concerns the geometric group, after forgetting Weil descent.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: The highest-weight constituent of IC_μ⋆IC_ν is IC_(μ+ν). A finite generating set for the rational polyhedral dominant monoid therefore reaches every simple; adjoining duals gives the required tensor generator for DM2.20.

For every nonunit simple, nμ grows in the torsion-free coweight lattice. The characteristic-zero finite-hull test DM2.22 rules out a nontrivial finite quotient of the reconstructed group. Apply this only after the MC.6 recognition hypotheses are checked.

Import the finite-type characteristic-zero reductivity criterion of ReductiveGroups Layer6. A nontrivial unipotent arithmetic Frobenius action on a constant multiplicity space is not ruled out by geometric semisimplicity.
acceptance: For G a torus, the simples are its lattice characters and the reconstructed group is the connected dual torus.
A two-dimensional trivial geometric object may have a unipotent Frobenius matrix; arithmetic semisimplicity is not a conclusion.
Do not apply the characteristic-zero connectedness or reductivity tests to a mod-ℓ fibre.

sources.match: The geometric semisimple category gives finite type, connectedness and reductivity before integral recovery.

sources.locator: §2, Proposition2.20 pp24–25, Corollary2.22 p26, Proposition2.23 pp26–27

nodes.title: Minuscule fibres and integral invariant ranks
nodes.statement: For G=PGL₂ split over an algebraic closure of F_p and n=2d, let f:Y_n→Gr be the n-fold minuscule convolution, Z_n=f^−1(1), and B₁ the minuscule Satake object. If Y_n is the smooth perfected iterated P¹-bundle of dimension n and f is proper semismall, then Hom(1,B₁^{⋆n}) is canonically BM_n(Z_n,Λ)(−d). This module is free with basis the d-dimensional irreducible components of the reduced fibre. Its rank is independent of ℓ and equals the characteristic-zero invariant multiplicity in the n-fold tensor power of the SL₂ standard module. For odd n the Hom group is zero by the component grading.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: The geometric GS2 input is only smoothness, properness and the semismall dimension bound; no modular decomposition theorem or modular Hom formula is assumed. Work on compatible finite-type deperfections and then transport étale cohomology through perfection.

Write B₁^{⋆n}=Rf_*Λ[n](d). Proper base change for exceptional pullback and smooth duality give Hom(δ₀,Rf_*Λ[n](d))=H^n(Z_n,i_Y^!Λ)(d). With K_Z=i_Y^!Λ[2n](n), this is H^−n(Z_n,K_Z)(−d)=BM_n(Z_n,Λ)(−d). Equivariance adds no extra morphisms for these objects by the existing connected-loop equivariance comparison.

Semismallness gives dim Z_n≤d. Duality and top compact cohomology identify its top Borel–Moore group with a free module on its d-dimensional components (after the displayed twist). There is no torsion contribution from smaller strata. Passing between Q_ℓ and F_ℓ preserves the rank.
Over Q_ℓ use the already geometric generic PGL₂→SL₂ identification to identify this rank with dim(V^{⊗n})^{SL₂}. This uses the generic result, not the integral rank-one statement being repaired.
acceptance: n=0 gives rank1.
n=2 gives rank1, the alternating SL₂ tensor.
n=4 gives rank2 and n=6 gives rank5; these Catalan values remain the same in characteristic two.
Odd n lies in the nonneutral component and gives no unit morphisms.

sources.locator: VI.11 pp236–237, rank-one reduction; VI.7.3 p219
sources.match: The rank-one proof needs an all-coefficient invariant test; connected equivariance makes the nonequivariant Hom calculation applicable.
The convolution dimension theorem supplies the geometric semismall input. The modular Hom identification is the duality argument given here, not a claim of Zhu's rational decomposition theorem.

nodes.title: Characteristic-two rank-one repair
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic two and H⊂SL₂ a closed subgroup scheme containing the diagonal torus. Suppose its irreducibles are uniquely indexed by their nonnegative highest weights and, for the standard module V, dim(V^{⊗n})^H equals the characteristic-zero SL₂ invariant multiplicity for every n. Then H=SL₂. In particular these strengthened hypotheses, supplied by the preceding geometric invariant calculation, repair the characteristic-two use of FS VI.11.2 in the integral PGL₂ identification. The highest-weight condition alone is insufficient.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: After a high Frobenius image H becomes reduced. Its identity component contains the torus, so is the torus, a Borel or SL₂. Negative highest-weight characters exclude the torus and Borel cases unless the reduced image is N(T). If the reduced image is SL₂, dimension and closedness imply H=SL₂. Otherwise H⊂H_a=(F^a)^−1N(T) for some a≥0.

Put n=6·2^a−2. The requested LP3 tilting identities give T(n)=A⊗T(4)^[a], with A=T(2^{a+1}−2)=St_a⊗St_a for a≥1 and A=k for a=0. The Steinberg module is self-dual and absolutely irreducible on the a-th Frobenius kernel, so A^{G_a}=k with trivial residual SL₂ action. Therefore T(n)^{H_a}=T(4)^{N(T)}.

T(4) has good-filtration character ∇(4)+∇(2). It has no SL₂ invariants, since the ∇(0)-multiplicity is zero, but its torus-zero-weight space has dimension2. The Weyl element is an involution in characteristic two, hence has a nonzero fixed vector there. Thus T(4)^{N(T)}≠0.

V^{⊗n} is tilting and contains T(n) as a highest-weight direct summand. On all other summands H_a-invariant dimensions are at least SL₂-invariant dimensions, while on T(n) they are strictly greater. Good-filtration theory makes the SL₂ invariant dimension of V^{⊗n} the characteristic-zero trivial multiplicity. This contradicts the geometric rank calculation because H⊂H_a.

The precise tilting, kernel and subgroup-classification interfaces are requests to their owners; the characteristic-two repair remains a recorded gap until those contracts are supplied. No prime-to-ℓ Donkin theorem is used for this purpose.
acceptance: N(T) in characteristic two satisfies the simple highest-weight uniqueness condition but fails the tensor invariant test at n=4.
For a=1 use n=10, A=T(2)=St₁⊗St₁; for a=0 use n=4 directly.
The corresponding odd-characteristic normalizer has a nontrivial sign character of highest weight0 and already fails highest-weight uniqueness.

sources.locator: LemmaVI.11.2 p237 and the PGL₂ proof pp236–237
sources.match: The printed characteristic-two highest-weight inference fails for the torus normalizer; tensor invariants provide the strengthened criterion.

sources.locator: Lemmas1.1 and1.4 pp3–4; Steinberg-square calculation p18
sources.match: These give the SL₂ tilting factorization and the character of T(4).
Steinberg kernel irreducibility, good-filtration invariant dimensions and tilting direct-summand/tensor properties supply the requested modular representation input.

nodes.title: Recovering the integral Chevalley model
nodes.statement: After base change to the completed maximal unramified ℓ-adic DVR O, the generic identification G^∨_K≅Ĝ_K and the integral torus and rank-one maps identify G^∨_O with the split Chevalley group Ĝ_O. First prove this for G_ad, whose dual has simply connected derived group. For a general G recover the central information by the π₁(G)-grading and its diagonalizable group, which may have torsion. This uses the existing RG2.3 extension principle and general Prasad–Yu criterion and RG2.4 integral-point generation, not a new lattice-existence theorem.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: The integral torus and simple rank-one Levi images contain the generators of Ĝ(O), hence Ĝ(O)⊂G^∨(O). Choose a generic faithful representation coming from a Satake object and retain its existing finite-free Satake lattice F(A). The point inclusion already makes this lattice Ĝ(O)-stable.

The smooth-group extension principle extends Ĝ_K→GL(F(A)_K) over O. Prasad–Yu makes it a closed immersion when ℓ≠2 or Ĝ_K has no geometric normal SO_(2m+1) subgroup. Apply first to the dual of G_ad, whose simply connected derived group satisfies this exception at ℓ=2.

Now G^∨→GL(F(A)) factors through the closed subgroup Ĝ: equations of Ĝ vanish on its generic fibre and O[G^∨] is flat. Every point of the smooth Ĝ_k lifts to O; the integral-point inclusion lifts it further to G^∨(O). Density of these points in the reduced Ĝ_k makes O[Ĝ_k]→O[G^∨_k] injective.

Apply the flat-module saturation criterion to the coordinate map, which is generically an isomorphism and injective modulo ℓ, to get the integral isomorphism. Faithfully flat descent returns to Z_ℓ. Recover general G from G_ad and the refined component grading; D(π₁(G)) is diagonalizable, not automatically a torus.
acceptance: The torus must be included among the integral-point generators in semisimple rank zero.
At ℓ=2 a generic odd orthogonal factor is a real exception to the closed-immersion criterion; it is not suppressed.
The lattice comes from a Satake object; no arbitrary maximal bounded subgroup assertion is needed.

sources.match: The integral recovery uses the integral-point inclusion, the closed-immersion criterion and the flat coordinate comparison.

sources.locator: Corollary1.3 p2; proof §5.4 p12; published Corollary5.2
sources.match: The source criterion has the residue-characteristic-two odd-orthogonal exception. Its general statement is already planned in the current upstream RG2.3 README.

nodes.title: Flat-module saturation criterion
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, π∈R and f:M→N a linear map. Suppose multiplication by π is injective on M and N, f becomes an isomorphism after inverting π, and the induced map M/πM→N/πN is injective. Then f is an isomorphism, without finite-generation assumptions. In particular this applies to flat modules over a DVR with uniformizer π. An executable equivalent hypothesis for localization surjectivity is that every y has π^n y=f(x) for some n and x, and localization injectivity says f(x)=0 implies π^n x=0 for some n.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: Localization injectivity and π-torsion-freeness of M give injectivity of f.
For y choose n minimal with π^n y=f(x). If n>0, reduction modulo π makes x divisible by π. Divide x=πz and cancel π in N to get π^(n−1)y=f(z), contradicting minimality. Hence n=0 and f is surjective.
acceptance: No Nakayama lemma or finite generation occurs.
The inclusion πR→R over a DVR is generically an isomorphism but fails injectivity modulo π, so is correctly excluded.
The conclusion is false if the π-torsion-free hypotheses are dropped; R→R⊕R/πR is a generic isomorphism and injective modulo π but is not surjective.

sources.match: The source proves the DVR flat-module case by saturation. The π-torsion-free formulation isolates exactly the elementary cancellation argument.

nodes.title: Descent of the geometric pinning
nodes.statement: The geometric generic identification and its integral recovery carry a canonical dual Cartan, Borel and simple-root lines on the divisor base. On the PGL₂ minuscule fibre the geometric simple-root line is Hom(H²(P¹),H⁰(P¹))=Z_ℓ(1). Transport by simple-Levi constant terms gives every root line; varying the auxiliary Borel and splitting extension descends the same pinned dual group with its geometric Weil action. A chosen square root of the transported Tate character identifies these root lines with the standard pinning.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: The cohomological grading and the weight filtration recover Cartan and Borel intrinsically. The rank-one cohomology calculation fixes the root line, including its Tate character.

Over the flag variety vary the Borel; its geometric simple connectedness makes the locally constant pinning data independent of that variation. Simple-Levi constant terms commute with this smooth base change.

Use the full-faithful locally constant Drinfeld realization, and then finite Galois descent through a splitting field, to descend the root-line data. Keep the root-line character intrinsic until the stalk-versus-parameter orientation is fixed.
acceptance: For a torus there are no root-line choices.
For PGL₂ the root line is Λ(1), whereas H²(P¹)=Λ(−1).
A choice of half Tate identifies pinning torsors; it is not a claim of a canonical square root of q.

sources.match: The pinning is built from rank-one root lines and descended through the locally constant realization.

nodes.title: The normalization cocycle
nodes.statement: Let σ:W→Aut(Ĝ) be the pinned action and let t:W→Ĝ be a continuous σ-cocycle lifting the adjoint grading cocycle: t(wv)=t(w)σ_w(t(v)). Put α_w=Ad(t(w))σ_w. The normalized comparison is the group isomorphism Ĝ⋊_αW→Ĝ⋊_σW, (g,w)↦(g t(w),w), with inverse (h,w)↦(h t(w)^−1,w). Thus if Φ(w) is the geometric Weil operator and ρ is its Ĝ representation, the pinned operator is Ψ(w)=ρ(t(w))^−1Φ(w). In Satake t=(2ρ̂)(κ), where κ is the square root of the transported root-line Tate character. Identifying κ(Frob_geom) with a scalar stalk convention remains the named Drinfeld orientation obligation.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.
For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.
Torsion coefficients are killed by an integer prime to p. ℓ-adic coefficients are obtained through compatible reductions; rational assertions are explicitly geometric.
proofSteps: The cocycle equation makes α an action. Multiply two elements on both semidirect-product sides and use t(wv)=t(w)σ_w(t(v)) to verify the displayed map.
The inverse is right multiplication by t(w)^−1, not conjugation by its adjoint image. Pull a geometric representation through this inverse to obtain Ψ=ρ(t)^−1Φ.

The grading cocharacter 2ρ̂ and a chosen square root κ provide a lift; changing κ by a quadratic character changes t by a central cocycle. This algebraic correction is valid before identifying the Drinfeld action with geometric-Frobenius stalk action.
acceptance: For t=1 the map is the identity.
On the central torus, a nontrivial central t still changes the W-section; conjugation would miss this change.
The formula with Ad(t(w)^−1)g generally fails the semidirect-product multiplication test.

sources.match: The corrected semidirect comparison is multiplication by the lifted cocycle.
A.6 supplies the grading twist; the conjugation formula of A.8 is corrected by the later lemma.

nodes.title: Levi transport of the half-Tate correction
nodes.statement: For a parabolic P with Levi M, compare the geometric normalized constant term with restriction of pinned dual representations. The discrepancy between G and M normalizations is the central M-dual cocycle (2ρ_G−2ρ_M)(κ(w)); in the FS parameter convention IX.7.1 the displayed cocycle is (2ρ_G−2ρ_M)(r)^{|w|}, with |Frob_geom|=1 and r²=q. The diagram commutes after the specified cocycle twist, including repeated Levi inclusions. The identification of the transported κ with this parameter convention is an explicit remaining obligation, rather than an assumed equality with the stalk half-Tate eigenvalue r^−1.

For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.

proofSteps: Apply the geometric constant-term tensor comparison before normalization. Subtract the two grading cocharacters to compute the relative cocycle, which centralizes ĤM.
Use the corrected semidirect isomorphism, not a conjugation formula, to transport both Weil operators. Under nested Levi inclusions the differences of 2ρ add, so the twists compose.
Record the positive exponent in IX.7.1 explicitly. A Drinfeld pullback/action-versus-stalk dictionary must account for it before identifying the same diagram with finite-field stalk traces.

nodes.title: Weil restriction and finite-index induction
nodes.statement: For a finite extension E′/E and G=Res_(E′/E)G′ choose an embedding E′→Ē. The pinned dual group is the product of conjugate copies of Ĝ′, with W_E permuting them. On the selected W_E′ factor, pullback to Div¹_E′ followed by the closed Grassmannian immersion and divisor pushforward corresponds to inflation along Ĝ⋊W_E′→Ĝ′⋊W_E′ and then finite-index induction to Ĝ⋊W_E. This is compatible with conjugating the chosen embedding, base change of legs, and the projection formula. Induction itself is not a strong monoidal functor. If f is the residue degree, q′=q^f and use r′=r^f.

For reconstruction use bounded-support ULA flat-perverse Satake objects, the parity-corrected fusion tensor and total cohomology; finite-projective continuous Weil fibres.

proofSteps: Fix the embedding before writing the projection onto a dual factor. The decomposition over Ē identifies the selected Grassmannian as a closed subspace; pull the leg divisor to E′ and apply the source pushforward.

The Weil finite-index pushforward is induction of the inflated representation. Check equivariance on every conjugate factor; another embedding conjugates both descriptions. The finite-set comparison is assembled factor by factor.
Use the projection formula Ind(U⊗Res V)=Ind(U)⊗V and the Mackey restriction formula. The dimension of Ind(1) is [E′:E], so there is no unqualified strong monoidal induction claim.

The degree of geometric Frobenius on W_E′ restricts to f times the E degree, giving r′=r^f. The full conjugate product still has [E′:E] factors; do not replace this degree by only the residue degree in ramified extensions.

A quadratic extension gives a two-factor dual product and induction of the trivial line has dimension2, whereas its tensor square has dimension4.
A totally ramified quadratic extension has f=1 and r′=r but still two conjugate factors.

The required foundational inputs are the relative classifying-stack base-change equivalence and the derived stable idempotent completion of the exact representation category, supplied by LP3/LP4. They must hold without inverting |Q| or π₁(Ĝ)_tors. GS4 owns this kernel application and HS1 consumes it. The conclusion is not full faithfulness or an equivalence with all enhanced sheaves.

nodes.title: Parity and half-Tate scalars
nodes.statement: For a commutative coefficient ring R define s_R(d)=1 when the integer d is even and −1 when it is odd. For a unit r define h_r(d)=r^(−d), the half-Tate scalar in degree d. For a finite set J of cohomological degrees and scalar stalk traces a_i, put T_R(ε,J,a)=s_R(ε)·Σ_(i∈J)s_R(i)a_i. For an actual stalk the finite sum runs over its cohomology, ε is its support parity and a_i is its geometric-Frobenius trace. The half twist of IC_μ in dimension d_μ multiplies its open-stratum trace by h_r(d_μ). These scalar operations do not construct sheaves or assert Frobenius descent.

proofSteps: Use integer parity, including negative cohomological degrees; finite sums make the formula meaningful in every commutative ring.
Evenness is additive modulo two, so support parity adds under tensor/convolution and the correction multiplies. Powers of the unit r define negative as well as positive half-Tate degrees.
For IC_μ=j_!*R[d](d/2), the open stalk lies in degree −d. Its cohomological sign is s_R(−d)=s_R(d); multiplying the support sign cancels it and leaves r^(−d).

Changing r to −r changes this coefficient by (−1)^d.
In characteristic two the two signs coincide, while the half-Tate scalar still matters.

nodes.title: Frobenius on bounded perfect models
nodes.statement: A trace realization for an unramified hyperspecial Satake object consists of a bounded finite-type special-fibre model with explicit Frobenius descent, and compatible realizations of its bounded convolution and constant-term correspondences. Require trace exchange for proper/compactly supported pushforward, tensor, and the Frobenius-equivariant perfection equivalences, with the stated Haar normalization. Given that data, the parity-normalized stalk trace is well-defined under compatible changes of realization, sends the unit to 1_K, and sends convolution to Hecke convolution. A model related only by an unspecified Frobenius power is not enough to define the same Frob_q trace.

nodes.title: Twisted Frobenius character
nodes.statement: Let L be a characteristic-zero coefficient field, Ĝ/L split pinned, σ a finite-order pinned automorphism and (V,ρ,Ψ) a finite-dimensional representation with Ψρ(g)Ψ^−1=ρ(σ(g)). For the ĤT-weight decomposition V=⊕_λ V_λ define ch_σ(V,Ψ)=Σ_(σλ=λ)Tr(Ψ|V_λ)e^λ in L[X^*(ĤT)^σ]. It is the restriction of the regular function gσ↦Tr(ρ(g)Ψ) on the Frobenius component. Under the existing SR4 restriction isomorphism this is a W_rel-invariant function on ĤT/(1−σ)ĤT. Nonfixed weight orbits contribute zero; no averaging or division by the order of σ occurs.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G/E is connected reductive and ℓ≠p.

proofSteps: For t∈ĤT, ρ(t)Ψ sends V_λ to V_(σλ). Its block trace is zero on every nontrivial σ-orbit, and on a fixed weight it is λ(t)Tr(Ψ|V_λ). This gives the displayed group-algebra polynomial.

Conjugacy invariance of the trace makes it descend through the twisted torus quotient. The existing SR4 Frobenius-component restriction theorem supplies W_rel invariance and the target algebra; GS4 does not reprove that invariant-ring theorem.

Trace on a direct sum adds; trace on a tensor product multiplies. Hence the construction is additive and multiplicative for compatible intertwining operators, whether or not Ψ is semisimple or has finite order.

An orbit of length greater than one has zero trace, not the sum of its weight dimensions.
Finite order of σ does not imply finite order of Ψ.

nodes.title: The geometric and spherical comparison square
nodes.statement: Let G/E be unramified, K hyperspecial and L contain a chosen unit r with r²=q. Use geometric Frobenius, vol(K)=vol(N(O_E))=1, positive valuations λ(π), and the SR4 transform S(f)(λ)=r^(−⟨2ρ,λ⟩)∫_N f(λ(π)n)dn. Given the finite-model trace adapter and the Drinfeld/parameter orientation adapter, S(τ_A)=ch_σ(V_A,Ψ_A) for every Frobenius-descended rational Satake object A, with Ψ_A its pinned normalized Weil operator. In the split IC basis with canonical open-stratum descent this is the ordinary highest-weight character χ_μ. It is a downstream comparison of the two existing constructions.

proofSteps: For a σ-fixed coweight λ put k=⟨2ρ,λ⟩. The constant-term weight space is H_c^k(S_λ,A)(k/2); if Φ_λ is the operator before this last twist, its normalized trace is r^(−k)Tr(Φ_λ). Support parity ε≡k modulo2 cancels the compact-support cohomological sign, and the scalar r^(−k) matches the Haar modulus.

The finite-model trace formula identifies that trace with the λ coefficient of S(τ_A). The orientation adapter identifies this normalized weight operator with the pinned Ψ_A. Nonfixed weights are permuted by Frobenius and contribute zero; the fixed-weight formula therefore proves the nonsplit equality without an absolute-weight orbit sum.

SR4 already constructs the normalized spherical transform, its invariant target and Frobenius-component restriction. Import its injectivity/isomorphism to get the comparison square; do not use the comparison as an input to SR4 or to dual reconstruction.

For split IC_μ, purity and the canonical constant-sheaf descent yield the normalized weight multiplicities and hence χ_μ. Its leading stalk coefficient is r^(−d_μ). Thus S(1_(KμK))=r^(d_μ)χ_μ plus lower dominant characters, with no lower terms for minuscule μ.
acceptance: For a split torus, the delta function at λ(π) maps to e^λ.
For GL₂ and μ=(1,0), the raw transform of the minuscule indicator is qX₁+X₂ and the normalized transform is r(X₁+X₂); τ_IC=r^−1 times that indicator gives X₁+X₂.
For PGL₂ minuscule P¹, the positive/negative weight trace scalars before the last constant-term twist are r,r^−1. The matching twists r^−1,r give normalized coefficients1,1.
For the nonsplit swapped-weight test, the permuted pair contributes0.

sourceIssues.reason: For G=1, take ℓ=3 and α=(3+4i)/5 in Q̄₃. It is a 3-adic unit, so geometric Frobenius↦α extends continuously from Z to Gal(F̄_q/F_q) for q of characteristic≠3. Both complex conjugates have absolute value1, so this one-dimensional representation is semisimple and pure of weight zero. But α has monic minimal polynomial x²−(6/5)x+1 and is not an algebraic integer, hence not a root of unity. Its image is infinite. Thus it is not in the finite-quotient subcategory already for the trivial group.
